papers.title: Digital-Twin-driven textile classification and foreign object recognition in automated sorting systems
papers.summary: The increasing demand for sustainable textile recycling requires robust automation solutions capable of handling deformable garments and detecting foreign objects in cluttered environments. This work presents a digital twin–driven robotic sorting system that integrates grasp prediction, multi-modal perception, and semantic reasoning for real-world textile classification. papers.title: Estimating the Causal Impact of Social Navigation Signals in Corridor Scenarios
papers.summary: Deploying robots in human-shared environments requires deciding not only how to navigate, but also when dedicated social signals are worth emitting. Classic observation-based inference can be misleading in such settings: confounding factors may bias the estimated relationship between a signal and the task outcome, leading to incorrect decisions. papers.summary: Touch is often attributed to the skin, but what if hard structures above the contact surface play a larger role than we thought? papers.title: Augmenting colonoscopy with artificial intelligence and robotic assistance: a human-factors scoping review toward a task-based shared autonomy paradigm
papers.summary: Colonoscopy is central to colorectal cancer prevention but remains a high-demand psychomotor and cognitive procedure, characterized by operator dependency, variable performance, and substantial physical and mental workload. Increasing evidence links procedural quality and safety to clinician-related factors, including musculoskeletal strain, fatigue, and non-technical skills. Concurrently, artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic technologies are emerging as potential tools to address these limitations. papers.title: Comparative operative performance of three robotic platforms in benign gynecologic surgery: a single-surgeon retrospective cohort study
papers.summary: This single-surgeon retrospective cohort study compared operative efficiency and perioperative outcomes among the da Vinci Xi, Hugo RAS, and da Vinci SP platforms in 218 women undergoing robotic hysterectomy or myomectomy for benign disease. The primary outcome was console time; secondary outcomes included operative time, estimated blood loss, length of stay, and complications.
